Queen's University Belfast GREAT Scholarships 2026 is an opportunity offered by Queen's University Belfast in partnership with the British Council and the GREAT Britain Campaign for students from India who aspire to pursue postgraduate courses in Law at the university. A minimum award of £10,000 for a year of study will be awarded to two selected students.
To be eligible, an applicant must:-
be a citizen or permanent resident of India
be available to start their academic studies at Queen’s by the start of the academic year in September 2026
meet the eligibility criteria of one of the following programmes:
LLM International Commercial and Business Law
have applied for and been offered a full-time place at Queen’s on your selected programme
not have been awarded a full or partial scholarship, studentship, or other government award to complete their studies
The selected scholars will receive £10,000 towards tuition fees for a one-year master’s programme.
Academic transcripts, including marksheets and certificates

A personal statement of less than 500 words explaining why the applicants are applying for a GREAT scholarship for an LLM programme at Queen’s University Belfast and how it will support their future career
Eligible candidates can apply by following these steps:-
Click on the 'Register' button and fill in the required registration details. (
If already registered, log in using Gmail/Mobile number/Email ID).
section and click the application link.
Fill the application form with relevant details and submit it.
Candidates must have an offer of a place to study an LLM Programme at Queen’s University Belfast for 2026 entry before completing the application form for the scholarship.
Applicants should apply for admission at least 4 weeks in advance of this date to allow sufficient time for a decision to be processed.
The selection of the candidates will be made based on academic merit, fulfilment of the eligibility criteria and the personal statement.
The Study UK team must be informed of any other scholarships awarded to a GREAT scholar in the same academic year.
be willing to establish an engagement with the UK as a scholar through personal and academic fulfilment.

be willing to attend events or participate in other activities organised by Study UK and the British Council for all UK-based GREAT scholars, including social media activities to discuss experiences and capture perceptions of studying in the UK.
be willing to maintain contact with the British Council and act as an ambassador for the GREAT Scholarships by sharing experiences of studying in the UK with future GREAT scholars
act as an alumnus of the GREAT Scholarships, and be willing, occasionally, to speak to potential candidates about his or her own experience of studying in the UK.

Source of Information: Buddy4Study app compiles details on scholarships/fellowships from government websites and private scholarship sources. Links to the official sources accompany each listing detail pages.
